FINAL IVX VENDOR-INDEPENDENCE AUDIT
MAP EVERY API, SDK, TOOL, SERVICE, CREDENTIAL, DEPENDENCY, AND RORK CONNECTION
REMOVE RORK 100% FROM IVX HOLDINGS WITHOUT BREAKING PRODUCTION

EXECUTE END TO END — DO NOT RETURN ONLY A SUMMARY

OBJECTIVE

Create a complete technical map of every API, SDK, package, service, webhook, domain, database, repository, credential, deployment pipeline, automation, AI provider, analytics tool, payment connection, mobile dependency, and Rork-controlled component currently used anywhere in the IVX Holdings project.

Then migrate, replace, remove, or transfer every Rork dependency so IVX Holdings can operate, build, deploy, update, monitor, and recover entirely under the owner’s accounts and control.

The final architecture must have:

- 0% Rork ownership
- 0% Rork-only runtime dependencies
- 0% Rork-controlled repositories
- 0% Rork-controlled deployment hooks
- 0% Rork-controlled credentials
- 0% Rork-controlled databases
- 0% hidden Rork SDKs
- 0% Rork branding or banners
- 0% vendor-locked build requirements
- 100% owner-controlled source code
- 100% reproducible builds outside Rork
- 100% documented infrastructure
- 100% tested production continuity

Do not remove anything blindly.
Map first, classify risk, migrate safely, test, deploy, and verify.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — COMPLETE PROJECT INVENTORY
==================================================

Audit the complete project, including:

- GitHub repositories
- Git branches
- Git submodules
- package workspaces
- Expo application
- React Native application
- web application
- backend services
- APIs
- database
- storage
- authentication
- AI services
- autonomous workers
- dashboards
- admin modules
- investor modules
- buyer modules
- CRM
- reels
- chat
- portfolio
- wallet
- transactions
- notifications
- analytics
- monitoring
- CI/CD
- mobile builds
- production domains
- DNS
- certificates
- secrets
- environment variables

List every application and service separately.

For every application provide:

- application name
- purpose
- source path
- repository
- branch
- framework
- runtime
- build command
- start command
- deployment target
- production URL
- owner
- current vendor dependency
- migration status

==================================================
PHASE 2 — MAP EVERY API
==================================================

Search the entire codebase for every API call.

Search for:

- fetch(
- axios
- ky
- got
- XMLHttpRequest
- GraphQL
- Supabase client
- RPC calls
- WebSocket
- EventSource
- SSE
- webhook URLs
- REST clients
- generated API clients
- native networking modules
- environment-based URLs
- localhost URLs
- hardcoded URLs
- hidden proxy URLs
- Rork URLs
- Vercel URLs
- Render URLs
- Supabase URLs
- AWS URLs
- Expo URLs
- GitHub URLs
- third-party service URLs

For every API endpoint document:

- service name
- base URL
- complete route
- HTTP method
- source file
- line number
- calling module
- purpose
- request schema
- response schema
- authentication method
- credential variable
- timeout
- retry behavior
- rate limit
- production status
- owner
- whether Rork controls it
- replacement plan
- removal risk

Create one API dependency table.

Required columns:

API ID
Service
Base URL
Endpoint
Method
Called From
Purpose
Authentication
Credential Variable
Data Sent
Data Received
Current Owner
Rork Dependency
Replacement
Migration Status
Verification Evidence

==================================================
PHASE 3 — MAP EVERY SDK AND PACKAGE
==================================================

Audit:

- package.json
- package-lock.json
- yarn.lock
- pnpm-lock.yaml
- bun.lock
- Podfile
- Podfile.lock
- Gradle files
- Android manifests
- iOS configuration
- Expo plugins
- native modules
- browser packages
- backend packages
- build plugins
- GitHub Actions
- Docker files

For every dependency document:

- package name
- installed version
- direct or transitive dependency
- used by which file/module
- purpose
- runtime or development only
- native code requirement
- license
- maintenance status
- security status
- Rork-owned or Rork-specific
- replacement package
- removal risk
- migration action

Search specifically for package names or code containing:

- rork
- rork-ai
- rork-sdk
- rork-api
- rork-runtime
- rork-client
- rork-generated
- rork-platform
- rork-deploy
- rork-auth
- rork-storage
- rork-chat
- rork-build
- rork-project
- vendor-specific unknown packages

Do not assume a package is safe because its name does not contain “Rork.”
Trace who publishes and controls it.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — MAP EVERY TOOL AND EXTERNAL SERVICE
==================================================

Audit every integrated service, including:

- GitHub
- Render
- Supabase
- AWS
- Expo
- EAS
- Apple App Store Connect
- Google Play Console
- Vercel
- Cloudflare
- email provider
- SMS provider
- payment provider
- bank integration
- escrow integration
- analytics provider
- crash reporter
- logging provider
- AI model provider
- OpenAI
- authentication providers
- file storage
- CDN
- video hosting
- image optimization
- push notifications
- map services
- KYC provider
- AML provider
- e-signature provider
- CRM integrations
- social-media integrations
- webhook consumers
- scheduled jobs
- monitoring tools
- autonomous-worker infrastructure

For every service provide:

- service name
- business purpose
- account owner
- billing owner
- login owner
- organization/workspace
- project identifier
- API key variable
- webhook
- callback URL
- domains
- data stored
- production dependency
- backup/export method
- Rork access level
- required transfer action

==================================================
PHASE 5 — CREDENTIAL AND SECRET OWNERSHIP MAP
==================================================

Do not expose secret values.

Audit only:

- variable name
- service
- environment
- where stored
- who controls it
- where loaded
- last verified use
- scope
- expiration
- rotation support
- whether Rork has access
- migration requirement

Audit all secret locations:

- Render environment variables
- Supabase secrets
- GitHub Actions secrets
- Expo/EAS secrets
- AWS Secrets Manager
- Vercel variables
- local `.env` files
- CI configuration
- database configuration
- mobile build profiles
- Android signing
- Apple signing
- webhook secrets

Classify every credential:

OWNER_CONTROLLED
SHARED_WITH_RORK
RORK_CONTROLLED
UNKNOWN
REVOKE_AFTER_MIGRATION

Do not request new credentials unless runtime evidence proves the existing credential is missing, expired, revoked, deleted, or returns 401/403.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — REPOSITORY OWNERSHIP
==================================================

Audit every repository referenced by the project.

Including known repositories such as:

- ibb142/rork-global-real-estate-invest
- ibb142/Ivxholding-2
- ibb142/rork-testing-app
- ibb142/rork-ivxholding--1
- any hidden, archived, forked, mirrored, generated, or deployment repositories

For every repository provide:

- repository URL
- owner
- visibility
- default branch
- active branch
- production connection
- latest commit
- contributors
- deploy keys
- GitHub Apps
- webhooks
- Actions workflows
- branch protections
- Rork access
- migration decision

Identify the single canonical production repository.

Remove production dependency on all obsolete or Rork-controlled repositories after verification.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — SOURCE-CODE RORK SWEEP
==================================================

Search all files for:

- Rork
- rork.com
- rork.app
- rork project IDs
- Rork API URLs
- Rork SDK imports
- Rork environment variables
- Rork headers
- Rork authentication
- Rork analytics
- Rork deployment hooks
- Rork banners
- Rork branding
- Rork generated comments
- Rork build scripts
- Rork proxy endpoints
- Rork callback URLs
- Rork storage
- Rork telemetry
- Rork feature flags
- Rork-specific metadata

Report every match with:

- repository
- file
- line
- match
- purpose
- runtime impact
- removal action
- replacement
- test required

Do not delete generated-code comments unless confirmed safe.
Prioritize runtime and ownership dependencies.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — BUILD-SYSTEM INDEPENDENCE
==================================================

Prove the project can be built without opening or using Rork.

Required builds:

Backend:
- install dependencies
- typecheck
- test
- build
- start locally or in an isolated environment

Web:
- install
- typecheck
- test
- build
- serve

Android:
- Expo/EAS or local Gradle build
- APK
- AAB
- install on physical device

iOS:
- local or EAS build
- archive
- TestFlight-ready artifact when Apple access exists

For every build provide:

- clean checkout
- required environment names
- exact command
- command output
- artifact
- checksum
- commit SHA
- build duration
- dependency on Rork: YES/NO

Acceptance:

A new developer or autonomous IVX worker must be able to clone the owner repository and build the complete app without Rork.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — DEPLOYMENT OWNERSHIP
==================================================

Map every deployment path:

GitHub
→ CI
→ Build
→ Artifact
→ Render/AWS/EAS
→ Production

Audit:

- Render services
- deployment hooks
- GitHub connections
- auto-deploy branches
- Docker registries
- EAS projects
- Expo organization
- AWS accounts
- Vercel projects
- mobile signing
- domains
- certificates
- DNS

For every production service provide:

- service ID
- account owner
- repository
- branch
- build command
- start command
- deployment hook owner
- current commit
- rollback method
- Rork access
- owner migration status

Replace every Rork-owned deployment hook with an owner-controlled hook.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — DATABASE AND STORAGE OWNERSHIP
==================================================

Audit all databases and storage systems:

- Supabase projects
- schemas
- tables
- views
- functions
- triggers
- RLS
- storage buckets
- realtime channels
- backups
- migrations
- service roles
- external databases
- Redis
- queues
- file storage
- video storage
- logs

For every database provide:

- project ID
- region
- account owner
- billing owner
- production purpose
- backup status
- migration history
- Rork access
- export method
- disaster-recovery plan

Verify the owner can:

- export all data
- restore all data
- apply migrations
- manage RLS
- manage backups
- revoke Rork
- continue production without Rork

==================================================
PHASE 11 — AI AND AUTONOMOUS-SYSTEM MAP
==================================================

Map every AI pathway:

- IVX IA Chat
- intent router
- senior-developer worker
- autonomous queue
- model provider
- prompt templates
- tool bindings
- job ledger
- proof ledger
- agent identities
- 12 senior agents
- planned 50-agent factory
- memory or retrieval systems
- embeddings
- vector storage
- AI usage metering

For every AI component document:

- source file
- API/provider
- model
- account owner
- credential variable
- routing logic
- fallback
- tool access
- Rork dependency
- independent replacement path

Prove IVX IA can execute without the Rork user interface.

The owner must be able to operate IVX IA from:

- IVX native app
- IVX web chat
- owner dashboard
- documented API

==================================================
PHASE 12 — DOMAIN AND NETWORK MAP
==================================================

Audit:

- ivxholding.com
- chat.ivxholding.com
- api.ivxholding.com
- all subdomains
- temporary domains
- Render domains
- Expo domains
- Vercel domains
- Rork preview domains
- AWS domains
- CDN domains
- webhook domains

For each domain provide:

- registrar
- DNS provider
- record type
- destination
- certificate
- expiration
- account owner
- Rork dependency
- migration action

Remove all production traffic through Rork-controlled domains or proxies.

==================================================
PHASE 13 — MOBILE APP VENDOR SWEEP
==================================================

Audit Android and iOS for:

- Rork SDKs
- Rork package names
- Rork app ownership
- Rork update URLs
- Rork OTA channels
- Rork signing keys
- Rork deep links
- Rork URL schemes
- Rork analytics
- Rork splash screens
- Rork branding
- Rork build profiles
- Rork project identifiers

Verify:

- Android package name belongs to IVX
- iOS bundle identifier belongs to IVX
- Expo project belongs to the owner
- Apple app belongs to the owner
- Google Play app belongs to the owner
- signing credentials belong to the owner
- update channels belong to the owner

==================================================
PHASE 14 — SECURITY AND ACCESS REMOVAL
==================================================

After migration and verification:

- remove Rork GitHub collaborator access
- revoke Rork GitHub Apps
- revoke Rork deploy keys
- remove Rork Render access
- remove Rork Supabase access
- remove Rork AWS access
- remove Rork Expo access
- remove Rork Apple access
- remove Rork Google Play access
- rotate credentials previously visible to Rork
- regenerate deployment hooks
- rotate webhook secrets
- rotate signing secrets only when required
- invalidate obsolete tokens
- remove unknown service accounts

Do not revoke access until the replacement path is proven.

Create a before/after access-control matrix.

==================================================
PHASE 15 — SAFE MIGRATION ORDER
==================================================

Use this order:

1. Inventory everything.
2. Confirm owner access.
3. Back up source, database, secrets metadata, and build artifacts.
4. Establish canonical repository.
5. Establish owner-controlled CI/CD.
6. Replace Rork deployment hooks.
7. Replace Rork APIs/SDKs.
8. Verify backend independently.
9. Verify web independently.
10. Verify Android independently.
11. Verify iOS independently.
12. Verify database and storage.
13. Verify domains and SSL.
14. Verify IVX IA and autonomous workers.
15. Run full regression.
16. Deploy controlled release.
17. Monitor production.
18. Revoke Rork access.
19. Rotate exposed credentials.
20. Run a final independence test.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — FULL REGRESSION AFTER REMOVAL
==================================================

- owner login
- member registration
- investor registration
- buyer registration
- landing page
- CRM
- investor pipeline
- capital pipeline
- portfolio
- wallet
- transactions

- Autonomous Dashboard
- IVX IA Senior Developer
- Android
- iOS
- web
- backend APIs
- database
- storage
- deployments
- monitoring

No Rork service may be contacted during the test.

Capture network logs and prove zero runtime requests to Rork domains.

==================================================
PHASE 17 — DISASTER RECOVERY
==================================================

Prove IVX can recover without Rork.

Required recovery test:

- clone clean repository
- restore environment configuration
- restore database backup in isolated environment
- build backend
- build web
- build Android
- start services
- run smoke tests
- verify owner login
- verify critical data
- verify IVX IA
- deploy to an isolated recovery target

Document recovery time and required owner-controlled accounts.

==================================================

==================================================

Return:

1. COMPLETE APPLICATION MAP
2. COMPLETE API MAP

4. COMPLETE EXTERNAL-SERVICE MAP
5. COMPLETE CREDENTIAL-OWNERSHIP MAP
6. COMPLETE REPOSITORY MAP

11. COMPLETE RORK-DEPENDENCY LIST

13. FILES CHANGED
14. PACKAGES REMOVED
15. APIS REPLACED
16. HOOKS REGENERATED

18. ACCESS REMOVED
19. BUILD EVIDENCE
20. DEPLOYMENT EVIDENCE
21. REGRESSION RESULTS
22. NETWORK PROOF OF ZERO RORK REQUESTS
23. DISASTER-RECOVERY RESULTS
24. FINAL OWNER ACCESS MATRIX

==================================================

==================================================

[ ] The owner can continue development and deployment independently.
